artists.biography:
The band was formed in Birmingham by Richard March, formerly with the group Pop Will Eat Itself, and Mike Stokes, with guest appearances by James Atkin, a member of indie band EMF. "Both more or less penniless, they drank in the same pub and were forced to buy their records at the cheapest place possible - car boot sales". Their live drummers were Keith York and Fuzz Townshend, alongside whom March previously played in Pop Will Eat Itself.

BRA signed on the Brighton based record label Skint and released their eponymous debut album, Bentley Rhythm Ace in 1997, which spawned the popular single "Bentleys Gonna Sort You Out!".

A second album, For Your Ears Only, was released in 2000 on Parlophone but was less popular. A further single "Madam, Your Carriage Awaits" was released. The group also compiled a two CD FSUK compilation album. In 2004, the Bentleys released a 4-song record with Sophia Lolley called Angel Face.

The name probably refers to the Rhythm Ace line of analogue drum machines manufactured by Ace Tone, some of which were rebranded and distributed by Bentley Pianos in the UK.

The group epitomises the big beat era. Signed to Skint Records, they enjoyed commercial success with their music being used on television advertisements and having an underground following.

The group split in 2000, but they played the occasional low-key DJ set. However, in 2009, they reformed and managed by Cut La Roc signed to Rocstar Records.

perplexity.description:
Bentley Rhythm Ace is the self-titled debut album by British electronic duo Bentley Rhythm Ace, released in 1997 on the Skint and Parlophone labels, with EMI involved in distribution. The album showcases a distinctive electronic style characterized by eclectic sampling, breakbeats, and playful, retro-inspired rhythms, blending elements of big beat and dance music prevalent in the UK electronic scene of the late 1990s. Its sound is marked by quirky, sample-heavy tracks that combine humor with energetic beats, reflecting the duo’s background as DJs and producers from Birmingham.

This debut album holds a significant place in Bentley Rhythm Ace’s discography as their breakthrough release, reaching number 13 on the UK Albums Chart and earning a Gold certification in the UK. It spawned notable singles such as "Bentleys Gonna Sort You Out!" which contributed to the album’s commercial success. Critically, the album was well received, with strong reviews from outlets like NME (9/10) and Pitchfork (8.4/10), praising its inventive production and infectious energy. It remains the duo’s most acclaimed and commercially successful work, preceding their less popular follow-up album, For Your Ears Only (2000).
